topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and outlines how previously learned concepts will be integrated.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition through pattern recognition receptors and inflammasomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infection and tissue damage using molecular patterns, receptor families, and intracellular signaling structures.

topics.label: Inflammatory response, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells direct immune cell migration into tissues, manage lymphatic drainage, and can trigger severe systemic pathology such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how acute inflammation is terminated, how tissues are repaired, and how the body adapts to persistent stimuli through chronic inflammation and granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the talk and previews the next lecture on the complement system.
